The strict second derivative -1/(1+t)^2 of log(1+t) orders all adjacent secant slopes; the exact adjacent log-score difference proves unique maximizers and endpoint ties for every theta>0. Rational grid collisions follow from tau^2=k/j and reduced fractions a/b; coprimality proves both single-sign site families recur exactly when a,b>1, while irrationality eliminates collisions. As all thresholds tend to zero, the sign-reversal iff follows. Python checker reproduces selected probability and tie tests; the infinite proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Section 2.4.6 of the 2026 DADL primary full text gives half-line unimodality and a finite candidate-selection method, not the all-parameter global modal staircase or the arithmetic iff for infinitely many unique sign reversals. The symmetric sign-magnitude law of Alyami et al. 2025 and two-sided geometric law of Kozubowski–Inusah 2006 do not imply this merged linear-geometric classification. Nine actual published-result searches and targeted literature aliases produced no stronger covering source. Strict concavity and elementary divisibility are known tools; priority risk of a missed or rephrased theorem remains and is recorded.
residual_risks: A direct or reparameterized modal-staircase classification might exist in unindexed literature; absence from published-result searches is not a novelty proof.

value.rationale: Exact population modal locations and multiplicities are natural shape invariants for signed-count distributions, directly complementing the primary paper’s incomplete practical global-mode prescription. The formula identifies every phase boundary and all persistent equal-height cases, and a sharp non-obvious fact: with tail-asymmetry fixed, the sign of the unique global mode can reverse infinitely many times as concentration tends to zero. The result supplies a model-interpretation constraint without alleging changes to mean, skewness, inference or sample-size behavior.
